title: RICIS-III: Gap-closure plan for singularity resolution (0/0, infinity)
scope_note: Tasks are limited to the mathematical core of RICIS (singularity axioms) and its formal verification in Lean. Goal is to actually close technical gaps, not to reformulate the claims.

tasks.problem: The central identity resolveRICIS(F.zeroF.det RExpr.zero RExpr.zero G.infF) is not definitionally equal (rfl failed, line 62). The theorem carries sorryAx. The declared TRUSTED_AXIOM has no basis in any configuration.
tasks.action: Construct a new proof of the identity without relying on rfl: either build an explicit simp/unfold chain with intermediate lemmas about F.zeroF.det/G.infF, or accept that the current A6-bridge formulation does not cover this case and reformulate the lemma.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: exit 0, no sorryAx, #print axioms for Jacobian_singularity_resolved contains no sorryAx.
tasks.estimate: not estimated -- verify the identity by hand before coding

tasks.problem: import Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic references a module that does not exist in the pinned Mathlib revision (correct path is Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic). File does not elaborate. No metadata, no trustStatus, no run record.
tasks.action: 1) Fix the import to Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic in a NEW version of the file (do not touch source bytes). 2) Create ricis-yang-mills.json with trustStatus. 3) Add to the MATHLIB_ARTIFACTS allowlist. 4) Run through the kernel and record the actual outcome.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Artifact receives a status based on an actual kernel run, not on the header claim in the file.
tasks.known_content_risk: Even after the import fix: current file content is a 2x2 determinant identity (f'/g' via skew_product), unrelated to gauge fields or the mass gap. Fixing the import yields compilation, not a substantive link to the problem.

tasks.problem: ricis_general_resolution is proved via dsimp of its own definition ricis_eval_general (tautology). ricis_reduce is declared but used by no theorem -- there is no link between 'structural reduction of a singularity' and 'evaluating the value'. The singularity condition N(a)=0 and D(a)=0 is never asserted for the general case.
tasks.action: 1) Formulate and prove a lemma linking ricis_reduce S to ricis_eval_general S for the case where S is actually singular at point a. 2) Explicitly exhibit the object being resolved (the singularity itself), not just the reduction mechanism.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: A new theorem that uses ricis_reduce in both its statement and its proof.
blocks: README/adopters.md should not characterize the current version of this file as a 'general resolution of singularities' until this task is closed.

tasks.problem: ax_A4_general and ax_SP1_general are declared as axiom (trusted contracts), not proved. The name ricis_equals_classical_limit creates the impression of a proved coincidence with the classical limit, although no limit expression is ever defined (and P1 forbids limits inside Resolve_RICIS).
tasks.current_status: Contracts confirmed as actual dependencies (#print axioms), but not proved as lemmas
tasks.action: 1) Either prove A4_general and SP1_general from more basic axioms (A1-A10, SP1-SP5) instead of postulating them. 2) Or explicitly mark them as contracts/hypotheses in the source itself (not only in JSON metadata) and rename ricis_equals_classical_limit to something that does not imply a proved coincidence.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Either 0 declared axioms in the file, or explicit in-source marking plus renaming of misleading theorem names.

tasks.artifact: src/model/initialMap.ts + all map nodes referencing *-ast-bridge artifacts
tasks.problem: Verified theorems prove structural AST identities (ricisReduce(divSelf e) = one), while map nodes referencing the same hashes phrase this as a solution to Riemann/Navier-Stokes/Jacobian/Yang-Mills.
tasks.action: For every map node referencing a *-ast-bridge artifact: rewrite the label/description so it describes the actually-proved statement (structural AST reduction), moving any reference to the external problem into a separate, explicitly informal field.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: No LEAN_VERIFIED node phrases an open external mathematical problem as solved.

tasks.problem: Static review of Lean code without an actual compiler run is unreliable (example: an incorrect prediction that the omega tactic was unavailable).
tasks.action: Add a rule to AGENTS.md: any claim about a Lean file's status requires an actual kernel run before being recorded in any registry; predictions without a run are explicitly marked UNVERIFIED_PREDICTION.

explicitly_out_of_scope: Physical construction of devices (Monolith, vortex engine) -- not part of the mathematical core.
Decoding of the Voynich manuscript -- not part of the mathematical core.
Claims about third-party companies 'adopting' the methodology (adopters.md) -- a communications question, not an engineering task.
